clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 60s presented with approximately 2 years of progressive spastic paraparesis manifesting as gait imbalance, frequent falls, severe thoracic and lumbar back pain, and leg spasms. Weakness began in the left leg and progressed to the right, notably with complete absence of sensory symptoms. Physical examination confirmed upper motor neuron pathology with hyperreflexia in all four extremities, positive Babinski reflexes bilaterally, and a positive left-sided Hoffman reflex, despite normal muscle strength (5/5) and intact cranial nerves. After 1.5 years of symptoms, advanced imaging with CT myelogram and MRI of the thoracic spine identified an arachnoid web at vertebral levels T7-T8, characterized by minimal dorsal indentation of the spinal cord and a positive scalpel sign without associated syrinx, prompting neurosurgical referral.
